name: Kiai

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 2009. *Leo Tuai: a comparative lexical study of North and Central Vanuatu languages. Pacific Linguistics 603. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-603
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 C59 2009
sources.note: Sec. 3.5 Vara Kiai (pp.27-28): phoneme inventory, orthography, PNCV>Kiai consonant/vowel changes; NO statement of Kiai stress (Clark gives one for Mota, Raga, Nokuku, etc., but not Kiai). Only indirect: 'Unstressed initial *a- > e-: *abé-na > epe-na, *ʔaváto > evato' with stress marked on PNCV etyma, plus sec. 2.1.3 p.16 'Word stress in PNCV was most likely on the penultimate vowel.'

sources.note: 'Orthography' pp.1-2: sound-symbol list (consonants with allophones, 5 vowels, diphthongs), 'My Kiai orthography is probably not phonemic, though it is not far from being so'; nothing on stress or accent; no stress marks anywhere in the ~50-page wordlist.
